summary: Pinned bundle and frozen test evidence hashes match. The recorded checks cover baud-rate behavior, manifest schema validation, invalid hardware startup, and repeated sim start/status/stop. Required evidence is missing for config-file loading and recovery after a deployment startup failure, so the accepted scope is not fully verified.
findings: The bundle SHA256 matches 8da5d76c5b1a54f0243ce90e46c420be49e4acfd39a3ad2bf029939a06a6fe95; the recorded server evidence matches 84186550616d89dfead433fa4424b3c34f209996f3b7bae9216b75d86955a54c. Checkout evidence pins soc-ap to the requested candidate commit.

Recorded positive and negative coverage includes PTY opens at 921600/460800/115200, rejection of 123456, CLI invalid-baud rejection, schema validation, missing-hardware-device rejection, and two successful sim lifecycle cycles.

The contract requires verifying that deploy_twin.sh reads aisoc_twin.conf and supports --config. The lifecycle command uses default settings and CLI overrides, but does not supply a distinct config file or verify config-derived values and precedence.

The contract claims recovery after startup failure. The evidence exercises failed preflight and ordinary stop/restart, but does not force a failure after daemons launch (such as a failed health check) and verify cleanup. The --foreground path also uses exec after launching background services, so its failure cleanup is not demonstrated.
accepted_scope: Software and PTY verification of the pinned TWIN-43 candidate: baud defaults and supported rates, invalid-baud rejection, manifest schema checks, hardware missing-device rejection, and repeated sim lifecycle. Physical hardware HIL is explicitly outside this contract’s acceptance scope and is not established by software tests.
unexecuted: Exercise --config with non-default values and confirm the loaded settings plus CLI override precedence.

Force a post-launch startup or health-check failure and verify all started processes and PID/runtime files are cleaned up; include the foreground failure path if it is within the intended acceptance scope.
Physical hardware HIL remains unexecuted and is outside the accepted software/PTY scope.
